text: The year was 1893, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city looming nearby was Paris, the country known for the Eiffel Tower, whose iron skeleton was rapidly reshaping the skyline and threatening to swallow the remaining wild spaces whole.
